title: Vit-Pytorch: Hierarchical Feature Distillation — Reproducibility & Deployment
text:
4.1 Definitions
A Vision Transformer processes an image as a short sequence of patch tokens rather than a dense grid. Given an image \(I \in \mathbb{R}^{H\times W\times C}\) splitted into \(N = HW / p^2\) non-overlapping patches of side \(p\), the model computes a sequence of \(N+1\) \(d\)-dimensional tokens (including a learnable [CLS] token) and applies \(L\) transformer blocks on top (Dosovitskiy et al. 2021).
Three concepts are central to our pipeline:

Masked Autoencoder (MAE). During stage 1, we randomly mask a large fraction \(m\) of the patches (here \(m = 0.75\)) and train the Teacher to reconstruct the normalised pixels of the masked patches (He et al. 2022). This yields strong local features without any labels.
REPA (Representation Alignment). During stage 2, while fine-tuning with ImageNet labels, we additionally force an intermediate ViT layer to align with the features of a frozen DINOv2 backbone (Oquab et al. 2024). The alignment loss is computed through a small MLP projection head and acts as a semantic bottleneck, distilling global structure into the Teacher.
Dynamic token pruning. Following Rao et al. (2021), the Student (DynamicViT) inserts lightweight prediction modules (“Predictor-LG”) at layers \(\{4, 7, 10\}\). Each predictor outputs a keep/drop score per token; uninformative patches are progressively pruned, compressing the computation. The target cumulative keep ratio at layer \(\ell_k\) is \(\rho^k\), with base ratio \(\rho = 0.7\).

The Student is trained with the composite loss from src/train/dynamic_loss.py:
\[
\mathcal{L}
  = \lambda_{\text{cls}}\,\mathcal{L}_{\text{CE}}
  + \lambda_{\text{kl}}\,\mathcal{L}_{\text{KL}}(s / T, t / T)
  + \lambda_{\text{distill}}\,\mathcal{L}_{\text{feat}}
  + \lambda_{\text{ratio}}\,\mathcal{L}_{\rho},
\]
where \(\mathcal{L}_{\text{CE}}\) is the classification loss, \(\mathcal{L}_{\text{KL}}\) is a temperature-scaled Kullback–Leibler divergence between the Student logits \(s\) and the Teacher logits \(t\) (Hinton et al. 2015), \(\mathcal{L}_{\text{feat}}\) distills token-wise features on the surviving tokens, and \(\mathcal{L}_{\rho}\) penalises deviations from the target keep ratios.

title: Vit-Pytorch: Hierarchical Feature Distillation — Reproducibility & Deployment
text:
4.2 Data used
All experiments target ImageNet-1k at 128×128 resolution, loaded from the Hugging Face hub dataset benjamin-paine/imagenet-1k-128x128 through data/load/imagenet_loader.py. The loader:

downloads (once) the train/validation splits into the HF_DATASETS_CACHE directory specified in .env;
applies a RandomResizedCrop(128, scale=(0.7, 1.0)) + horizontal flip + ImageNet normalisation on the training set, and a plain resize + normalisation on validation/test;
splits the official train split into 90 % train / 10 % validation using a fixed seed (generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(50)), so the split is deterministic across machines.

A few samples are bundled under data/images/ so the site can render thumbnails without touching the Hugging Face hub:

Figure 1: A few training samples from data/images/. The number in the filename is the integer ImageNet class id.





To make the tokenisation step tangible, we can split one of these samples into the same 16×16 patch grid that the ViT actually sees, and then display what a random 75 % MAE mask looks like:


Show code
rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=0)
patch = 16
img_path = sample_files[0] if sample_files else None

if img_path is not None:
    img = np.asarray(Image.open(img_path).convert("RGB").resize((128, 128)))
    H, W, _ = img.shape
    nh, nw = H // patch, W // patch

    grid = img.copy()
    for i in range(1, nh):
        grid[i * patch - 1 : i * patch + 1, :, :] = 255
    for j in range(1, nw):
        grid[:, j * patch - 1 : j * patch + 1, :] = 255

    n_tokens = nh * nw
    keep_mask = rng.random(n_tokens) >= 0.75
    masked = img.copy()
    for k, keep in enumerate(keep_mask):
        if keep:
            continue
        i, j = divmod(k, nw)
        masked[i * patch : (i + 1) * patch, j * patch : (j + 1) * patch] = 128

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(12, 4))
    for ax, im, title in zip(
        axes,
        [img, grid, masked],
        ["Original 128×128", f"{nh}×{nw} patch grid", "MAE mask (75%)"],
    ):
        ax.imshow(im)
        ax.set_title(title)
        ax.axis("off")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()








Figure 2: Left: the original image. Center: the 8×8 patch grid used by the Teacher (128/16 = 8 patches per side). Right: a random 75 % MAE-style mask applied at the patch level — this is the actual input the SSL Teacher is trained to reconstruct.

title: Vit-Pytorch: Hierarchical Feature Distillation — Reproducibility & Deployment
text:
4.3 Training pipeline
The pipeline is a three-stage hierarchical feature distillation scheme:

Stage 1 — SSL pre-training (train_teacher_SSL.py). A ViT-Base Teacher is trained with an MAE objective on 75 %-masked patches, with a decreasing layer-wise learning-rate decay to prioritise early layers and capture local textures.
Stage 2 — Supervised + REPA fine-tuning (train_teacher.py). The SSL Teacher is fine-tuned with ImageNet labels, while an intermediate layer is aligned with frozen DINOv2 features through a small MLP head and a cosine similarity loss. Layer-wise learning-rate decay is now increasing, prioritising deep layers and the classification head.
Stage 3 — Student distillation + dynamic pruning (train_student.py). A DynamicViT Student is initialised from the Teacher’s weights and trained with the composite loss defined above. Predictor modules at layers 4, 7, 10 learn which tokens to drop so that the per-image compute decreases while classification accuracy is preserved as much as possible.

Running the full pipeline from the project root:
python -m src.train.train_teacher_SSL  --dataset imagenet --mask_ratio 0.75
python -m src.train.train_teacher      --dataset imagenet \
    --resume-from checkpoints/imagenet/ssl_teacher/ssl_teacher_best.pth
python -m src.train.train_student      --dataset imagenet --rho 0.7 \
    --run_name tiny_dynamic_vit

section: 4.5 Reproducibility of our code and experiments
text:
4.5 Reproducibility of our code and experiments
We followed the main principles of reproducibility in scientific research for Machine Learning:

Deterministic train/val split. The 90/10 split is performed with torch.Generator().manual_seed(50) in data/load/imagenet_loader.py, so two different machines produce the exact same split.
Pinned dependencies. requirements.txt lists every transitive dependency with an exact version; uv.lock plays the same role for the uv resolver.
Versioned configuration. All hyper-parameters are Python modules under configs/, versioned alongside the code. Changes to these files are visible through git blame / git log.
Versioned checkpoints. A curated subset of trained weights is committed to checkpoints/public/imagenet/ (SSL Teacher, Teacher, and Student at \(d_{\text{model}} = 128\), \(p = 16\)), so that any reader can bypass training and run inference directly.
Versioned artefacts. The TensorBoard event files, loss curves and pruning visualisations displayed in this report live under logs/ and are part of the repository, hence the figures above are regenerated by the CI at every push.
Continuous deployment/publication. A GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/quarto.yml) renders this .qmd on every push to the reprod branch and publishes the result to GitHub Pages.

section: 5.1 Input data specification and output format
text:
5.1 Input data specification and output format

Input. A single image (PIL, NumPy or Torch tensor) with three RGB channels, any resolution. The preprocessing pipeline will resize it to 128×128 and standardise it with the ImageNet statistics used during training.
Output. A Python dictionary:

logits: torch.Tensor of shape (1, 1000) — raw class scores over ImageNet-1k.
top5: a list of (class_id, probability) pairs, sorted by probability, with class ids matching the ImageNet-1k ordering.
keep_masks: a list of three binary masks (one per pruning index) of shape (1, N) with \(N = (128/p)^2\) tokens. Useful to visualise which regions the Student actually looked at.

title: Vit-Pytorch: Hierarchical Feature Distillation — Reproducibility & Deployment
text:
5.2 Pre-processing pipeline
The same torchvision transforms used at test time (see data/load/imagenet_loader.py) must be applied:
from torchvision import transforms as T

IMAGE_SIZE = 128
MEAN = [0.485, 0.456, 0.406]
STD  = [0.229, 0.224, 0.225]

preprocess = T.Compose([
    T.Resize((IMAGE_SIZE, IMAGE_SIZE)),
    T.ToTensor(),
    T.Normalize(mean=MEAN, std=STD),
])

5.3 Running a forward pass
import torch
from PIL import Image

from src.models.dynamicViT import DynamicVisionTransformer

# 1. Load the public Student checkpoint shipped with this repo.
ckpt_path = "checkpoints/public/imagenet/d128patch16/student/student_epoch_120.pth"
ckpt = torch.load(ckpt_path, map_location="cpu")

# 2. Rebuild the exact architecture the checkpoint was trained with.
#    Hyperparameters are persisted inside the .pth by train_student.py.
student = DynamicVisionTransformer(**ckpt["hyperparameters"])
student.load_state_dict(
    {k.replace("_orig_mod.", ""): v for k, v in ckpt["model_state_dict"].items()},
    strict=False,
)
student.eval()

# 3. Run on a new image.
img = Image.open("data/images/sample_7.png").convert("RGB")
x   = preprocess(img).unsqueeze(0)                 # (1, 3, 128, 128)

with torch.inference_mode():
    logits, _feats, keep_masks, _scores = student(x)

probs   = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
top5_p, top5_i = probs.topk(5)
print(list(zip(top5_i[0].tolist(), top5_p[0].tolist())))
The returned keep_masks can be overlaid on the input to reproduce the style of visualisation shown in Figure 7.

6.1 GitHub Actions workflow
Two workflows live under .github/workflows/:

quarto.yml — renders this report with Quarto on every push to the reprod branch, then publishes the resulting static site to the gh-pages branch. The build installs dependencies with uv sync, so the CI uses the exact same lockfile as contributors.
ruff.yml — runs the ruff linter/formatter on every push and PR to main, using the configuration in ruff.toml (88-char line length, double quotes, imports sorted).

title: Vit-Pytorch: Hierarchical Feature Distillation — Reproducibility & Deployment
text:
6.2 Tests
The src/test/ directory acts as a small integration-test suite that can be run manually after training:

parameters_computing.py — loads both checkpoints and computes the exact FLOPs, MACs and parameter counts with calflops.
compare_st-te.py — evaluates Teacher and Student on the ImageNet-1k test split, then regenerates the performance and confusion-matrix figures displayed above.
test_SSLteacher.py — reports MSE, MAE and PSNR for the MAE Teacher and re-renders the ssl_reconstruction_*.png visualisations.

A light-weight pytest entry point is declared in pyproject.toml ([scripts] test = "pytest") for future unit tests targeting the model building blocks.
